Vantorre CX-10 refurbished (2021, s/n VT21-30877) — repeat E34 lockouts since delivery. Posting now, our review window closes Thursday.

Unit: 10 x 1/1 GN, delivered and commissioned 14/09/2026, warranty registered to 14/03/2027.

Error history:
- SR-1190, 22/09: E34 steam generator low water level, intermittent lockout in both combi and steam mode. Level sensor replaced, 3 x steam cycles tested OK, no charge. The error log shows E34 x 9 since 14/09 — the fault was logging from day one of ownership, not from use.
- SR-1236, 06/10: steam generator found heavily scaled, descaled and flushed. Core probe recalibrated, now within 1 degree.
- 27/10: E34 again, further scale found, invoiced $280 + GST ($308). The unit was six weeks old and still inside the six-month parts and labour warranty.

Core probe: before 06/10 it was reading low. Lamb shoulder, oven 63 degrees against our ThermoPen 70, same result twice in the same cook. Within 1 degree since recalibration.

Water: our Fitzroy supply is soft. Melbourne Water quotes average hardness around 15 mg/L as CaCO3, among the softest in the country. Scale doesn't build up in three weeks on that. The generator was descaled and pressure tested at refurbishment (inlet 320 kPa OK at the 22/09 visit) and E34 was logging from the delivery date, so the scaling was in the unit when it arrived.

Service impact: Saturday 24/10, E34 locked us out at 6.10pm with 60 covers booked. Lamb finished on the stove and the deck oven, pork belly 86'd, and we ate the cost.

Credit where it's due: both warranty attendances were prompt, the sensor was replaced free of charge, and the probe recalibration was done properly. The problems are the repeat fault and a callout fee on a six-week-old unit still under warranty.

Other kitchens should know: a $15k unit can arrive with a scaled generator and a probe reading 7 degrees low, and neither is flagged in the listing.
